findings.evidence: SENT='Claim your energy rebate refund at {} before the deadline.'; U.has_link_or_contact(SENT.format('refunds-portal 丶ㆍᆢ shop/claim')) -> False (also for '丶丿乀 shop/claim', '丨丶丿 shop', 'ㆍᆢ丶 cash/claim', '丶丿乀乁 shop/claim', '丶ㆍᆢ online'); mask_links leaves it unchanged; SY.verify(SENT.format(link)[:-1]+' [1].',[src]) keeps the claim with no drop; SY.extractive('energy rebate refund deadline',[src]) returns the sentence; build_surface(...) output contains 'refunds-portal 丶ᆞᆢ shop/claim' and require_valid passes. Cause: _separator_word returns len(set(word)) <= _MAX_FOREIGN (2), so a 3-distinct-letter foreign word becomes the 'name', the gap before 'shop' is a plain space (prose), and 'shop' is not in _CORE. Not listed among the owner-accepted residuals (only the bracketed separator is); D16 states 'a name, then anything at all, then a real TLD is a link'. Probes: /tmp/uri_review_R16/probe_links.py, probe_r16_01.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat any unbracketed word of a script different from both the name's and the ending's (or of the ending's script made of non-alphabet letters) as a separator regardless of its distinct-letter count, or bound by script-membership rather than letter count; owner to confirm the precision cost (e.g. 'Tokyo 東京都 is big' masked). Add a parametrised regression over 3- and 4-letter combinations of stroke/dot letters.
findings.title: R1-01 link class still open: a foreign-script separator word of three or more distinct dot/stroke-shaped letters ('丶ㆍᆢ', '丶丿乀', '丨丶丿', 'ㆍᆢ丶') between name and a non-core TLD is read as the name, so the link passes has_link_or_contact, mask_links, verify(), extractive(), the research surface and the A2UI validator (W1-AC12/AC15, D16)

findings.evidence: N.check_url('http://[64:ff9b:1:7f00:0:100:808:808]/') -> Target(...) accepted (127.0.0.1 in RFC 6052 /48 layout); 'http://[64:ff9b:1:a9fe:a9:fe00:808:808]/' (169.254.169.254 /48) accepted; /64 form 64:ff9b:1:0:7f:0:100:0 accepted via DNS answer and connected (helper probe /tmp/uri_review_R16/ssrf/p2_nat64.py, p4_fetch.py). ipaddress reports these as not global. 64:ff9b::/96 forms are correctly refused.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse 64:ff9b:1::/48 outright (local-use, not needed for public fetches), or check the embedded IPv4 at every RFC 6052 offset (/32,/40,/48,/56,/64,/96) and refuse if any is non-public; never return before the is_global check for the local-use prefix.
findings.title: netpolicy accepts 64:ff9b:1::/48 (RFC 8215 local-use NAT64) addresses embedding a private IPv4 at the /48, /56 or /64 offsets: _embedded_v4 always reads the last 32 bits and the NAT64 branch returns before the is_global check (W1-AC1)

findings.evidence: has_link_or_contact(SENT.format('refunds-portal ~ go ld/claim')) -> False; verify() keeps it, extractive() returns it, surface shows it. _endings rejects 'go'+'ld' via _COMMON2 regardless of the gap before the name.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the _COMMON2 exclusion only when the gap between name and ending is ordinary prose; join the split when the gap holds a non-prose character.
findings.title: Split ending whose first piece is a common two-letter word is not joined even after a non-prose separator ('refunds-portal ~ go ld/claim', '~ he lp') - the disclosed, not owner-accepted, limitation is wider than needed

findings.evidence: ResearchJob(..., providers=[SearxngProvider(base_url='http://\u2603.example')]).run() -> FAILED INTERNAL_ERROR (helper probe /tmp/uri_review_R16/ssrf/p9_searxng_job.py). Config-only trigger; not reachable from page content.
findings.suggested_fix: Catch httpx.InvalidURL (or httpx.InvalidURL plus ValueError) in the provider call and return FAILED/UNAVAILABLE for that provider.
findings.title: SearxngProvider does not catch httpx.InvalidURL: an owner-configured SearXNG URL with an invalid IDNA host turns the research job into FAILED INTERNAL_ERROR (R11-02 pattern in search)

findings.evidence: Helper probe /tmp/uri_review_R16/assist/p_toctou.py revokes between check_unchanged and the store: output 'access state: OFF / EMITTED after revoke: assist.answer COMPLETE ...' and the text stays in _answers; assist_ask_status blanks it on read; the UI's _early buffer keeps unknown-id events and _discardDerived does not clear it (code reading).
findings.suggested_fix: Re-check the stamp under the access lock at store/emit time and blank the result if changed; clear _early in _discardDerived.
findings.title: Assist answer stored and emitted after Stop: the ask thread re-checks the grant before, not under the lock with, storing and emitting the answer (A0-AC4 race)

No image is sent on refusal; the user still presses Ask.
